Immune system — innate and adaptive immunity

card.title: Immunity — innate barriers to antibody memory

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Innate immunity (skin, lysozyme, phagocytes, interferons) strikes everything foreign within hours; adaptive immunity (B-cell antibodies, T-cell killers) learns specific antigens and remembers them — the basis of vaccination (weakened/killed antigen trains memory without disease). Allergies are immunity overshooting (IgE, histamine); autoimmunity is immunity misfiring at self (rheumatoid arthritis, lupus). The syllabus pathogen parade (Plasmodium, dengue virus, Ascaris, Mycobacterium, HIV, ringworm fungus) maps each invader to its route and control.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: innate (birth, non-specific): barriers + phagocytosis + inflammation  ·  adaptive (acquired, specific): humoral (B→antibodies IgG/A/M/E/D) + cell-mediated (T-killer/helper)  ·  primary response: slow, weak · secondary: fast, strong (memory)  ·  allergy: IgE + mast-cell histamine  ·  vaccines: live-attenuated / killed / toxoid / mRNA

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Vaccination needs an immunogenic but safe antigen plus time for memory formation (booster schedules). Antibodies bind specific epitopes — mismatched antibodies do nothing. Herd immunity thresholds assume random mixing and durable immunity. Autoimmune diagnosis needs self-reactive markers, not just symptoms.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Malaria (Plasmodium via Anopheles, cyclical fever), dengue (Aedes, breakbone + platelet crash), TB (Mycobacterium, DOTS therapy), AIDS (HIV kills helper-T, treatment not cure), ringworm (dermatophyte fungus, not worm). Colostrum gifts newborns maternal IgA — borrowed adaptive immunity.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Why do vaccines prevent but rarely cure? Prevention pre-builds memory cells and circulating antibodies, so the real pathogen meets an armed secondary response (fast, overwhelming); curing an established infection must chase a replicating, sometimes latent enemy (HIV provirus, TB granulomas) that already outruns the same machinery.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Immunity is strain-specific (flu drifts yearly — new vaccines follow). Immunocompromised patients cannot take live vaccines. Allergies and autoimmunity show the system has no wisdom, only pattern-matching. Eradication worked for smallpox (no animal reservoir); most pathogens keep refuges.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From clonal selection: each lymphocyte carries one receptor specificity; antigen binding selects and expands its clone (primary = days, low titre) while survivors become memory cells (secondary = hours, high titre, higher affinity via somatic hypermutation). Vaccination runs this selection with a safe antigen — the derivation of every immunisation schedule.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Pathogen table: name → vector/route → symptom → control (five columns, ten rows — the unit's bank). Immunity answers: innate vs adaptive first, then humoral vs cellular. Allergy = IgE/histamine; autoimmune = self-attack (one example each).
